title: Ordinal-affinity routing with soft-threshold load shedding and latency-first failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a more graceful multi-region routing policy that prioritizes low-latency region choices while avoiding large-scale cross-region failovers during transient congestion. Current region selection is either strict geo-pin (hard affinity) or naive latency fallback which causes large blast radiuses when a region's autoscaler lags.

Proposal: Implement an 'ordinal-affinity' routing policy combined with soft-threshold load shedding and circuit-breaker hysteresis. Key ideas:
- Ordinal-affinity: keep an ordered list of preferred regions per tenant/request key (region A > B > C). Instead of hard pinning, requests attempt region A, but fallbacks are allowed within a short hedging window and only when capacity/latenct/slos indicate genuine degradation.
- Soft-threshold shedding: when a region nears a configurable soft-capacity threshold (e.g., 75% of target throughput for the tenant), shed non-critical traffic (batchable/low-priority) with a graceful 503+Retry-After rather than immediate global reroutes.
- Latency-first failover with budgeted hedging: use moving-window p95 latency + token-bucket budget per region to allow occasional hedges to lower-latency regions without exhausting failover budgets.
- Circuit-breaker hysteresis: open/close decisions should include minimum open time and progressive backoff, plus a fast-probe pathway that routes a small percentage of requests to the previously-open region to detect recovery.

Why different from existing steering rules: This ticket focuses on per-tenant ordinal preferences and soft, budgeted shedding (not binary pin/unpin), plus explicit hedging budgets to limit failover blast radiuses. The goal is to preserve low tail latency for high-priority traffic while protecting region stability and avoiding cascade autoscaler triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Config: new routing policy 'ordinal-affinity' available in runtime config and Console UI

Behavior: By default, requests go to first-preference region. On p95 latency > configured threshold for 1 minute OR available capacity below soft threshold, only non-urgent labels are shed. High-priority requests hedge within budget to lower-latency region.
SLOs: System-level test demonstrates <1% cross-region failover churn for tenant traffic during a simulated 30% capacity shortfall in primary region
Observability: Per-tenant hedging budget, region open/close events, shed counts and reasons are emitted to traces/metrics and appear in Console routing dashboard
Safety: Circuit breaker to open only after N consecutive region errors or sustained latency breach; automated fast-probe validates recovery before full close
design_decision: We chose ordinal-affinity over strict geo-pin because many workloads benefit from low-latency fallbacks, but hard pinning causes tail latency regressions when the pinned region degrades. Soft-threshold shedding avoids expensive autoscaler thrash by shedding less-critical work instead of mass rerouting. Hedging budgets cap the total cross-region traffic caused by failovers and give us predictable unit cost exposure.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime switch and per-tenant config. 2) Canary on internal tenants (10% of traffic) for 48h with verbose telemetry. 3) Expand to early customers who opt-in. 4) Gradually increase to 100% after 2 weeks of stability. 5) Post-rollout: run synthetic failure drills (node/zone pressure, region outage) to validate hysteresis and probe behavior.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit metrics: routing.hedge_attempts, routing.hedge_success, routing.shed_count{reason}, routing.circuit_state{region,tenant}, routing.hedge_budget_remaining. Alerts: >5% shed_count sustained over 15m for any tenant (investigate soft threshold tuning); hedge_budget_exhausted -> pager for oncall; circuit_open for >5m without recovery -> page.
